entries.text_preview: Generate a 10-second realistic video from this image. The person lifts the white ceramic mug slightly, brings it to the mouth, takes one natural sip, then lowers the mug and places it onto the wooden table. Keep the camera static and keep the full body, mug, hand, face, and tabletop clearly visible throughout the motion. The mug should remain in the person’s hand until it is placed on the table. Add realistic synchronized audio: a subtle sipping sound when the person drinks, followed by one clear ceramic mug contact sound when the mug touches the wooden table, with light indoor room ambience. No music, no speech.

You are inspecting a crop from a video of a person holding a mug. Goal: identify the *hand-mug contact region* on a clear confirmed grasp keyframe. Do NOT infer a new contact point from rim drinking or from unrelated body/rim pixels. Definitions: - object side means which semantic part of the mug is being touched by the hand. - handle means the C-shaped side loop attached to the mug. - rim means the top lip used for drinking; mouth-rim contact is not a hand-handle grasp. - If the hand/fingers are hidden, occluded, or not clearly on the handle, say contact_visible=false. - Ignore any debug overlays, colored circles, text, skeletons, or rendered proxy if present. Judge real image content only. Return ONLY compact JSON with these keys: { "contact_visible": true/false, "hand_side": "left_hand" | "right_hand" | "unknown", "contact_fingers": ["thumb" | "index" | "middle" | "ring" | "pinky" | "palm" | "unknown"], "primary_contact_finger": "thumb" | "index" | "middle" | "ring" | "pinky" | "palm" | "unknown", "object_part": "handle" | "body" | "rim" | "bottom" | "unknown", "object_region": "upper_handle" | "middle_handle" | "lower_handle" | "handle_inner" | "handle_outer" | "body_side" | "rim_front" | "rim_side" | "unknown", "handle_grasp_type": "pinch_handle" | "hook_handle" | "palm_support" | "body_grasp" | "not_handle_grasp" | "unknown", "contact_point_2d": [u, v] | null, "visible_evidence": "short visual evidence", "use_as_stable_grasp_keyframe": true/false, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "reason": "one short sentence" }

Create a simple 3D mug proxy from the clean mug reference image. This asset is for contact reasoning, not photorealistic reconstruction. Required semantic parts: - body - handle - rim - bottom Geometry requirements: - The body is a vertical cylindrical cup body matching the clean reference proportions. - The rim is a thin rounded ring. - The bottom is a flat circular base. - The handle is a separate semantic part named "handle". - The handle should be a smooth C-shaped side tube whose two endpoints enter/attach directly into the cup body. - Do not add external connector pads, wedge blocks, rectangular bars, ribbed joints, or mechanical-looking interfaces. - The handle must be consistent with the clean reference: when viewed from the side it should project like a narrow vertical curve/strip, not a large front-facing loop. Keep the geometry simple and robust. The downstream pipeline will convert this asset into proxy/mug_proxy.json and use the handle as the object-side contact region.

Use the attached multi-keyframe mug reference images to create a clean mug reference image for Articraft. Task: Remove the hand/fingers/arm occlusion from the mug and reconstruct the complete same mug. Important constraints: - Keep the same mug identity, color, scale, cylindrical body, rim, bottom, and side handle. - Preserve the camera perspective and viewpoint of the selected hand-holding frame. - Do not invent a different mug. - Do not change the table, background, or global scene geometry if they are present. - The handle must be visible and attached naturally to the mug body. - Use the multiple keyframes only to infer the occluded handle/body shape; do not blend multiple mugs into one inconsistent shape. Preferred output: A single clean image of the mug with hand removed, suitable as Articraft image-conditioned input.

Create a canonical 3D mug proxy for contact reasoning using the provided clean mug reference image. Requirements: - The mug is one rigid object. - Expose semantic parts named exactly: body, handle, rim, bottom. - The body is a simple vertical cylindrical cup body. - The handle is a smooth C-shaped side handle rigidly attached to the body. - The handle must be embedded/connected into the mug body at upper and lower attachment zones; do not leave gaps. - The handle is NOT an independently moving part and must not have its own joint motion. - The handle should be usable as the object-side contact region for a human hand. - The rim is a ring at the top of the cup. - The bottom is a flat disk/support region. - Prefer clean robust geometry and stable semantic parts over photorealistic detail. - Avoid decorative artifacts, blocky rectangular handles, disconnected handles, or changing the mug identity. The asset will later be aligned to video keyframes for 6D/weak-perspective pose fitting. Keep the geometry simple and metrically plausible.

Create a refined 3D mug proxy from the supplied zoomed reference montage. This is for contact reasoning, so preserve clean semantic parts and simple geometry, but do not make a crude block model. Required semantic parts: - body - handle - rim - bottom Geometry requirements: - The body is a vertical hollow cylindrical cup with smooth circular sides. - The rim is a thin rounded circular ring at the top. - The bottom is a flat circular base/disk. - The handle is a separate side part named handle. - The handle must be a smooth curved C-shaped loop attached to the cup side. - The handle should look like a real mug handle: rounded tube, two attachment pads, open inner hole. - Do not build the handle from rectangular bars or box primitives. - The handle should remain fixed relative to the mug body as a semantic contact region. Keep the object static and robust for downstream contact-region reasoning. Prefer a clean canonical mug with correctly named parts over decorative detail.

Edit the current mug model to fix the handle/body attachment. Current defect: - The handle has visible wedge-like attachment pieces outside the cup. - This still looks like an added connector instead of a mug handle grown into the cup. Required geometry change: - Remove all separate attachment pads, wedge pieces, connector pieces, fillets, and external transition blocks. - Make the handle a single smooth C-shaped tube. - Extend the two endpoints of the C-shaped tube directly into the cylindrical cup body. - The C-loop endpoints should penetrate the cup side wall by a small amount, so the tube visibly disappears into the body. - The visible connection should be just the tube entering the cup wall, not a separate interface object. - The upper and lower endpoint centers should be inside the body wall enough to pass connectivity checks. Do not add: - no pad geometry - no wedge geometry - no rectangular connector - no ribbed rings - no mechanical joint - no extra transition parts Keep: - exactly semantic parts: body, handle, rim, bottom - handle remains a separate semantic part named handle - smooth open C-shaped side handle - cylindrical cup body, flat bottom, rounded rim Validation target: - In the viewer, the C-shaped handle should look embedded into the mug body at two points. - The model should compile cleanly.

Edit the current mug model to fix the ugly mechanical-looking handle/body interface. Observed defect: - The handle attachment pads currently look like ribbed pipe fittings or threaded connectors. - This is wrong for a ceramic mug. Required fix: - Remove the ribbed/ringed/mechanical connector appearance at both handle attachment points. - Replace the current attachment pads with smooth, plain ceramic fused pads. - The handle should transition into the cup body with a short smooth oval/elliptical fillet-like pad. - The pad should be visually simple: no grooves, no rings, no repeated sectional ridges, no stacked cylinders, no screw/thread look. - Keep a slight physical penetration/overlap into the cup body so the handle is connected, but make the visible interface smooth and flush. Keep: - exactly semantic parts: body, handle, rim, bottom - handle remains a separate semantic part named handle - smooth C-shaped side handle with open hole - cylindrical cup body, flat bottom, rounded rim Validation target: - In the viewer, the mug should look like a normal ceramic mug proxy. - The handle/body interface should look fused, not like a pipe connector.

Edit the existing mug model only. Do not regenerate the mug from scratch. Keep the current continuous mesh-based C-shaped handle design based on `_c_shaped_handle_mesh`; do not replace it with boxes, segmented cylinders, or a blocky/mechanical handle. Goals: - Preserve the clean cylindrical mug body, torus rim, flat bottom, and continuous smooth C-shaped tube handle. - The mug remains one rigid object with semantic parts named exactly: body, handle, rim, bottom. - The handle remains a separate semantic part but fixed to the body by a fixed articulation. - Improve only the handle-to-body interface: make the upper and lower endpoints visibly embedded into the cup wall with no gap. - Preserve the natural C-shape and smooth tube appearance. - Avoid rectangular pads or mechanical-looking connectors. - If needed, slightly extend the handle mesh endpoints into the ceramic wall and add small smooth blended neck geometry, but keep it visually continuous with the handle tube. - Compile must pass with no warnings if possible. If overlap is intentional at the cup wall, justify it in tests. This asset is for contact reasoning: body, handle, rim, and bottom must remain semantically accessible; handle is the object-side hand contact region.

Edit the existing mug model so it matches the supplied zoomed mug reference more closely. Main problem to fix: - The handle must visibly and physically attach to the cup body. - Do not leave any visible gap between handle and mug body. - The upper and lower handle attachment pads must penetrate or overlap slightly into the side wall, like a fused ceramic mug handle. Reference-image requirements: - Keep the cup body proportions close to the reference image: simple vertical cylindrical cup, flat bottom, rounded top rim. - Keep the handle on the side shown in the reference and make it a C-shaped side loop. - The handle should be rounded and smooth, not rectangular bars. - The handle should have a clear open hole, but both ends must be anchored to the body. Semantic requirements: - Keep exactly these semantic parts: body, handle, rim, bottom. - The handle must remain a separate semantic part named handle for contact-region reasoning. - It is acceptable and preferred to add explicit scoped overlap allowances between body and handle pads, because a real ceramic handle is fused into the body. Validation target: - The compiler/viewer should show a single visually connected mug with no floating handle. - The handle/body connection should be obvious in camera view.
